body:
An external base type's cached pointer can be cleared during module cleanup. Deallocation already has a type-hierarchy fallback for that case, but the surrounding GC and heap-type checks still dereference the cleared pointer. An embedding host that cleans up a module while retaining an instance can therefore crash when the instance is destroyed.

Resolve the parent destructor and its GC and heap-type flags together through the existing type-hierarchy helper. This removes the direct call through the cached pointer when module state is disabled, adding a hierarchy walk to that path. The srctree regression invokes the module's cleanup callback through `PyModule_GetDef`, then releases a cyclic instance of an imported extension subclass. Calling the callback explicitly makes the finalization ordering deterministic while an instance survives cleanup.

The regression fails on master and passes with the fix. Checked with C and C++ inheritance/deallocation tests and the CPython limited API.

comment_data.body: The return value is obfuscating the signature and intention of the function. A better way to deal with such a need is to split the function in two and let both functions do _less_ rather than letting the one function do _more_.
Feel free to use an f-string here.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -2133,23 +2133,11 @@ def generate_dealloc_function(self, scope, code):
                     code.putln("PyObject_GC_Track(o);")
                 code.putln("__Pyx_PyType_GetSlot(%s, tp_dealloc, destructor)(o);" % base_cname)
             else:
-                if needs_gc:
-                    # We don't know if the base class uses GC or not, so must find out at runtime
-                    # whether we should undo the untracking above or not.
-                    code.putln("if (PyType_IS_GC(%s)) PyObject_GC_Track(o);" % base_cname)
-                # This is an externally defined type.  Calling through the
-                # cimported base type pointer directly interacts badly with
-                # the module cleanup, which may already have cleared it.
-                # In that case, fall back to traversing the type hierarchy.
-                # If we're using the module state then always go through the
-                # type hierarchy, because our access to the module state may
-                # have been lost (at least for the limited API version of
-                # using module state).
-                code.putln("#if !CYTHON_USE_MODULE_STATE")
-                code.putln("if (likely(%s)) __Pyx_PyType_GetSlot(%s, tp_dealloc, destructor)(o); else" % (
-                    base_cname, base_cname))
+                # The imported base type pointer may have been cleared during module cleanup.
+                code.putln("#if CYTHON_USE_TYPE_SPECS")
+                code.putln("int base_is_heap =")
                 code.putln("#endif")
-                code.putln("__Pyx_call_next_tp_dealloc(o, %s);" % slot_func_cname)
+                code.putln("__Pyx_call_next_tp_dealloc(o, %s, %d);" % (slot_func_cname, needs_gc))

comment_data.body: Split in [8fa03b8e1](https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8083/commits/8fa03b8e1c398b8e79917edf8abc679903382d54): the new `__Pyx_get_base_dealloc()` only looks up the base type. The generated deallocator reads its heap flag, re-tracks the object for GC when needed and calls the base `tp_dealloc` itself. After the split nothing used `__Pyx_call_next_tp_dealloc()` any more, so [5b33d2375](https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8083/commits/5b33d2375f469e009bfdcd8bd339b26a6def7b3f) removes it. `run.external_base_cleanup` and `exttype_dealloc` pass.
Done in [8fa03b8e1](https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8083/commits/8fa03b8e1c398b8e79917edf8abc679903382d54): the replacement line uses an f-string.

Split base deallocator lookup from invocation
